parameters.content:
## Every new product becomes a promo video

Takes ONE product - from a Google Sheet out of the box, or from your
Shopify catalogue in production - and renders it as a 1080x1920 promo
(~14 s): a hook scene with the product on a designed plate, an offer scene
with the tagline, price and a computed SAVE badge, then a shop-now card.
In sheet mode the video URL is written back to the row and the row is
marked done.

**No store needed to try it.** `source` is `sheet` out of the box, so a Zvid
key plus a Google account is the whole shopping list. Flip `source` to
`shopify` when you want it watching your real catalogue (blue note below).

### Setup (about three minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** - create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** - attach your Google credential to *Read products sheet*
   and *Mark row done*, then pick your spreadsheet and tab in both nodes.
   The columns are in the yellow note next to the sheet node.
3. **Open `Config`** - set `brandName`, `brandColor`, `brandAccent`,
   `storeUrl` and `shopNowText` to your brand.
4. **Run it - the first run renders for real and spends about 15 credits.**
   When it finishes, click **▶ Watch video** to play the promo here in n8n.
5. Free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the credit
   quote plus an **editorLink** to watch the draft, nothing spent and the
   sheet untouched. Set it back to `false` to render.
6. **Activate** - in `shopify` mode it checks for a new product every 30
   minutes. In `sheet` mode it takes one row per run.

## Your sheet: eight columns

Header row (row 1), spelled exactly like this:

| Title | Price | CompareAtPrice | ImageUrl1 | ImageUrl2 | Tagline | Status | VideoUrl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- **Title** and **ImageUrl1** are required. Everything else is optional.
- **ImageUrl1 / ImageUrl2** must be public http(s) URLs - Shopify CDN links
  are, and so is anything on your own CDN. With a second photo the offer
  scene shows a different angle; with one photo it re-frames the same shot
  inside a different plate. **Photos are never cropped** (see the green note).
- **CompareAtPrice** - fill it in and the offer scene strikes it through and
  adds a computed **SAVE x%** badge. Leave it empty and both disappear.
- **Tagline** - trimmed on a word boundary to `maxTaglineChars` (90). Empty
  falls back to `fallbackTagline` in Config.
- **Status** - leave EMPTY for products waiting to be rendered. The workflow
  takes the first empty-Status row and writes `done` + the video URL when the
  render finishes. Put anything in Status by hand to skip a row.

## Production path: your real Shopify catalogue

The sheet is the demo path so the template runs the minute it is imported.
To watch your store instead:

1. Shopify admin -> **Settings -> Apps and sales channels -> Develop apps**
   -> *Create an app* -> **Configure Admin API scopes** -> tick
   **`read_products`** -> *Install app* -> reveal the **Admin API access
   token** (it starts with `shpat_`). It is shown once - copy it now.
2. Add a second n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `X-Shopify-Access-Token`,
   value = that token. Attach it to *Poll new products* only.
3. In **Config** set `source: "shopify"` and `shopDomain` to just the
   subdomain (`my-shop`, not `my-shop.myshopify.com`).

This is the **webhookless** install: no app review, no public URL, no
Shopify Trigger node. *Poll new products* asks for the five newest products
every 30 minutes and compares the newest id against the last one announced,
kept in the workflow static data.

**The first Shopify run only seeds that marker** and renders nothing, so
turning the workflow on never floods your feed with your back catalogue.
The id is stored only AFTER a successful render, so a failed render retries.

## Product photography is never cropped

Store photos arrive in every aspect ratio there is - square, 4:5, 2:3, wide
lifestyle shots - and cropping one is how an automation ruins a product
page. *Build project JSON* places every photo **contained** inside a
designed plate: the whole shot fits, centred, never cropped and never
stretched. The plate (not the photo) carries the composition, and a hairline
is drawn on the photo's real edge so a white studio cut-out still reads as a
mounted print on the cream plate.

**Type scales with the copy.** A 26-character product name sets at 92 px; a
70-character one steps down to 58 px over three lines and the block below it
moves out of the way. The end card measures its own stack (ring, brand,
name, price, button, domain) and centres it, so a short name and a long one
both look composed.

**Colours stay legible whatever you put in Config.** Chip and button labels
pick whichever of your ink / paper / black / white contrasts best against
`brandAccent`, and the accent used as text on dark is nudged lighter until
it clears 3.5:1 - so a pale yellow accent gets dark labels automatically.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders for real.** Set it to
`true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates the
payload, quotes the exact credit cost and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the exact video and tweak anything by hand, with nothing
spent. **Neither the sheet row nor the Shopify marker is touched on a dry
run**, so the next real run renders the same product.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render and mark the row done.

## Publishing the video (optional tail)

The workflow ends with the video URL in *Run summary* (and in the sheet) -
a clean handoff you can extend after **Mark row done**:

- **Instagram / TikTok / everywhere** - pass `videoUrl` to a scheduler like
  Blotato, Buffer or Metricool via their HTTP API; they accept a public video
  URL directly, no download step needed.
- **YouTube Shorts** - add an *HTTP Request* node (GET the `videoUrl`,
  response format `File`) followed by the native **YouTube** node
  (Video -> Upload, binary `data`). Needs a YouTube OAuth2 credential.
- **Product page / meta ads** - drop `videoUrl` into your theme or ad
  platform via its own API.

They are left out of the required path on purpose so the template imports
and runs with a Zvid key and a Google account, nothing else.

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: n8n renders the downloaded MP4 as an inline
video player with a download button - the finished promo, no URL to copy.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (and `jobId`,
`creditsCharged`, `savePercent`) if you want to pipe the result onward.
